failure_summary.description: Answers used an expanded geographic/name form or listed alternatives instead of the expected single conventional label.
Agents missed the requested relation or returned only part of a work title despite existing scope guidance.
Malformed or flattened clue prompts were not reliably separated from adjacent metadata and search terms.

patch.reasoning: Clarify the conflicting guidance about using a person's longest supported identity: answer at the scope requested, without adding formal-name elements merely because a source contains them. Add a targeted rule for reconstructing flattened clue prompts. The relation and title-scope misses are already addressed by existing rules, so they do not warrant duplicating guidance.

edits.target: For people, use the full identity supported by substantive context; do not answer with only a surname merely because a clue echo abbreviates it. Preserve initials, titles, and other name elements when the clue or a reliable passage supplies them—do not strip them for stylistic normalization.
edits.content: For people, answer at the identity scope requested, using the conventional identifying name rather than the longest form found in a source. Do not add optional middle names, titles, or family or dynastic descriptors merely because a passage supplies them; retain name elements when they are conventionally part of the requested identification. Do not give only a surname when the clue calls for an identifiable person and the surname alone is ambiguous.

## Reconstruct Flattened Clue Prompts
When a question is keyword-like, has lost spaces or punctuation, or comes from a clue archive, do not assume every adjacent word belongs to one phrase. Use the source snippet and context to distinguish the clue from category labels, answer-length markers, and neighboring clue text. Identify the requested answer slot and answer that clue, rather than a related entity suggested by the surrounding terms.
